title: The Sharing Economy
passage: The sharing economy has grown from a niche idea into a global industry worth billions of dollars. Services that allow people to rent homes, cars, and tools from one another have made better use of resources that would otherwise sit idle. Supporters argue that this model reduces waste and creates flexible income. Critics, however, point out that it has disrupted traditional industries and raised concerns about regulation and worker protection.

questions.question: What does the sharing economy allow people to do?
questions.explanation: 共享经济让人们互相租用房屋、汽车和工具。

questions.question: What do supporters say about the sharing economy?
options: It reduces waste and creates income
questions.explanation: 支持者认为它减少浪费并创造灵活收入。

questions.question: What concern do critics raise?
questions.explanation: 批评者担心监管和工人保护问题。

title: The Effects of Sleep Deprivation
passage: Sleep deprivation has become a widespread problem in modern society, where long working hours and constant screen time push sleep to the bottom of the priority list. The effects are more serious than many realise. Lack of sleep impairs attention and memory, weakens the immune system, and increases the risk of serious illness. Researchers stress that consistently sleeping fewer than seven hours a night is linked to long-term health problems, and they urge people to treat sleep as a necessity rather than a luxury.

questions.question: What is a major cause of sleep deprivation mentioned in the passage?
options: Long working hours and screen time
questions.explanation: 长时间工作和持续的屏幕使用把睡眠挤到了优先级的最后。

questions.question: What is one effect of lack of sleep?
questions.explanation: 睡眠不足会削弱免疫系统。

questions.question: How many hours of sleep is linked to long-term health problems?
questions.explanation: 研究人员指出，长期每晚睡不到七小时与健康问题相关。

title: Urban Green Spaces
passage: As cities grow denser, the value of urban green spaces becomes increasingly clear. Parks and tree-lined streets do more than beautify a neighbourhood; they cool the surrounding air, absorb rainwater, and provide habitats for wildlife. Studies also link access to green space with lower levels of stress and better mental health. Despite these benefits, green space is often the first thing to be sacrificed when land is scarce, a decision planners increasingly regret.

questions.question: What is one physical benefit of urban green spaces?
questions.explanation: 绿地和林荫道能降低周围空气温度。

questions.question: What do studies link green space to?
questions.explanation: 研究把接触绿地与压力降低和更好的心理健康联系起来。

questions.question: What happens when land is scarce?
questions.explanation: 土地稀缺时，绿地往往首先被牺牲。

title: The Digital Divide
passage: The digital divide refers to the gap between those who have access to modern technology and those who do not. This divide exists not only between rich and poor countries but also within them, affecting the elderly, rural residents, and low-income families. During the pandemic, when education and work moved online, the divide became painfully visible, as students without reliable internet struggled to keep up. Closing this gap, experts argue, is essential for building a fair society.

questions.question: What does the digital divide refer to?
questions.explanation: 数字鸿沟指能接触现代技术的人与不能的人之间的差距。

questions.question: Who is affected by the digital divide?
options: The elderly, rural residents and low-income families
questions.explanation: 鸿沟影响老年人、农村居民和低收入家庭。

questions.question: When did the divide become painfully visible?
questions.explanation: 疫情期间教育和办公转为线上，数字鸿沟变得显而易见。

title: The Psychology of Gratitude
passage: Psychologists have found that gratitude is one of the simplest and most effective ways to improve well-being. People who regularly write down things they are thankful for report higher life satisfaction and fewer symptoms of depression. The practice works by shifting attention away from what is missing and toward what is already present. Experts recommend making gratitude a daily habit, such as noting three good things before going to bed.

questions.question: What is gratitude according to the passage?
options: An effective way to improve well-being
questions.explanation: 感恩是改善幸福感最简单有效的方法之一。

questions.question: How does gratitude work?
options: By shifting attention to what is present
questions.explanation: 感恩通过把注意力从缺失转移到已有而发挥作用。

questions.question: What do experts recommend before bed?
questions.explanation: 专家建议睡前记下三件好事。

title: The Rise of Remote Work
passage: Remote work, once a rare perk, has become a permanent feature of many industries. Employees value the flexibility it offers, saving hours previously spent commuting and gaining more control over their schedules. Employers have also noticed benefits, including access to a wider talent pool and lower office costs. However, remote work is not without challenges. Some workers report feelings of isolation, and managers struggle to build team culture across a screen.

questions.question: What do employees value about remote work?
questions.explanation: 员工看重远程工作的灵活性，节省通勤时间。

questions.question: What benefit do employers notice?
options: Access to a wider talent pool
questions.explanation: 雇主发现远程工作能接触到更广泛的人才库并降低办公成本。

questions.question: What challenge is mentioned in the passage?
questions.explanation: 一些员工报告感到孤立，管理者难以隔着屏幕建立团队文化。

title: Why We Procrastinate
passage: Procrastination is often mistaken for laziness, but psychologists see it differently. They describe it as an emotional problem rather than a time-management problem. When a task triggers anxiety or boredom, the brain seeks relief by turning to something more pleasant, and this short-term escape only makes the task loom larger. Breaking the cycle, experts say, begins with forgiving yourself for past delays and starting with a task so small that beginning feels easy.

questions.question: How do psychologists describe procrastination?
questions.explanation: 心理学家把拖延描述为情绪问题而非时间管理问题。

questions.question: Why does the brain turn to something more pleasant?
questions.explanation: 当任务引发焦虑或无聊时，大脑通过转向更愉快的事来寻求缓解。

questions.question: What is the first step to breaking the cycle?
questions.explanation: 专家说打破循环始于原谅自己过去的拖延。

title: Food Waste
passage: About a third of all food produced worldwide is never eaten. This waste occurs at every stage, from farms where crops are rejected for cosmetic flaws, to homes where leftovers are thrown away. The environmental cost is enormous, since wasted food consumes land, water, and energy, and its decomposition releases greenhouse gases. Reducing food waste, experts argue, is one of the most effective actions individuals can take to fight climate change, starting with simple habits like planning meals and using leftovers.

questions.question: How much of the world's food is never eaten?
questions.explanation: 全球约三分之一的食物从未被食用。

questions.question: Why are crops rejected on farms?
options: For being too small to pick
questions.explanation: 农作物因外观瑕疵而被丢弃。

questions.question: What is a simple habit to reduce food waste?
questions.explanation: 规划膳食和利用剩菜是减少浪费的简单习惯。

title: The History of the Internet
passage: The internet began as a research project in the 1960s, designed to allow computers at different locations to share information. At the time, few imagined it would become the global network it is today. Over the following decades, it expanded from universities and research centres to homes and businesses around the world. The arrival of the World Wide Web in the early 1990s made the internet accessible to ordinary people, and it has since transformed communication, commerce, and culture.

questions.question: When did the internet begin?
questions.explanation: 互联网始于 20 世纪 60 年代的研究项目。

questions.question: What was the original purpose of the internet?
questions.explanation: 互联网最初是为了让不同地点的计算机共享信息。

questions.question: What made the internet accessible to ordinary people?
questions.explanation: 20 世纪 90 年代初万维网的出现让普通人也能使用互联网。

title: The Science of Smell
passage: Of all the senses, smell is perhaps the most closely linked to memory. A single scent can instantly recall a childhood kitchen or a long-forgotten holiday. Scientists explain that this is because the brain region that processes smell sits directly next to the areas responsible for emotion and memory. This close connection is why certain smells trigger vivid recollections that other senses cannot match, a phenomenon sometimes called the Proust effect.

questions.question: Which sense is most closely linked to memory?
questions.explanation: 嗅觉是与记忆联系最紧密的感官。

questions.question: Why do smells trigger vivid memories?
options: The smell region is next to emotion and memory areas
questions.explanation: 处理嗅觉的大脑区域紧邻负责情绪和记忆的区域。

questions.question: What is this phenomenon sometimes called?
questions.explanation: 这一现象有时被称为普鲁斯特效应。

title: Volunteering and Well-being
passage: Volunteering is usually described in terms of what it gives to others, but research shows that volunteers themselves gain a great deal. Studies find that people who volunteer regularly report better mental health, lower stress, and a stronger sense of belonging. Helping others appears to activate the same reward systems in the brain that respond to other pleasures, leading some researchers to call volunteering a natural mood enhancer.

questions.question: How is volunteering usually described?
options: In terms of what it gives to others
questions.explanation: 志愿服务通常被描述为给予他人。

questions.question: What do regular volunteers report?
questions.explanation: 定期做志愿者的人报告更好的心理健康、更低的压力和更强的归属感。

questions.question: What do some researchers call volunteering?
questions.explanation: 帮助他人激活大脑的奖赏系统，研究者称之为天然的情绪提升剂。

title: Preparing for a Job Interview
passage: A job interview is as much about preparation as it is about first impressions. Experts advise candidates to research the company thoroughly, practise answering common questions, and prepare a few thoughtful questions of their own. During the interview, body language matters as much as words: eye contact, a firm handshake, and a confident posture all signal genuine interest. After the interview, sending a brief thank-you note can leave a lasting, positive impression.

questions.question: What should candidates do before an interview?
questions.explanation: 专家建议候选人充分研究公司，练习回答问题并准备自己的问题。

questions.question: What signals genuine interest during the interview?
questions.explanation: 眼神接触、有力的握手和自信的姿态都显示出真正的兴趣。

questions.question: What can leave a lasting impression after the interview?
options: Asking for a higher salary immediately
questions.explanation: 面试后发送简短的感谢信能留下持久的正面印象。

title: Reducing Plastic Pollution
passage: Plastic pollution has become one of the most pressing environmental problems of our time. Millions of tons of plastic enter the oceans every year, harming marine life and entering the food chain. Governments around the world have begun to respond, with many countries banning single-use plastic bags and straws. Individuals can also help by carrying reusable bags, refusing unnecessary packaging, and properly recycling the plastic they do use.

questions.question: What is one of the most pressing environmental problems?
questions.explanation: 塑料污染已成为当今最紧迫的环境问题之一。

questions.question: How do plastics harm the environment?
options: They enter the oceans and food chain
questions.explanation: 塑料进入海洋，危害海洋生物并进入食物链。

questions.question: What have many countries done?
questions.explanation: 许多国家禁止了一次性塑料袋和吸管。

title: Artificial Intelligence in Medicine
passage: Artificial intelligence is transforming the field of medicine in ways that were once the stuff of science fiction. AI systems can now analyse medical images, such as X-rays and scans, with remarkable accuracy, often spotting signs of disease that human eyes might miss. In some hospitals, AI assists doctors by suggesting diagnoses and treatment plans. While AI will not replace doctors, it is becoming an increasingly valuable tool that allows medical professionals to work faster and more accurately.

questions.question: What can AI systems do with medical images?
questions.explanation: AI 系统能以惊人的准确度分析 X 光片和扫描图像。

questions.question: How does AI assist doctors?
questions.explanation: AI 通过建议诊断和治疗方案来协助医生。

questions.question: What is the role of AI according to the passage?
questions.explanation: AI 不会取代医生，而是成为越来越有价值的工具。

title: The Benefits of Regular Exercise
passage: The benefits of regular exercise extend far beyond physical fitness. Exercise has been shown to reduce stress, improve mood, and even enhance cognitive function. When we exercise, the brain releases chemicals that create feelings of well-being, which is why many people describe exercise as a natural antidepressant. Experts recommend at least 150 minutes of moderate activity per week, but they stress that even small amounts of movement, such as a daily walk, can make a meaningful difference.

questions.question: What is one benefit of exercise beyond fitness?
options: It reduces stress and improves mood
questions.explanation: 运动能减轻压力、改善情绪甚至增强认知功能。

questions.question: What does the brain release during exercise?
questions.explanation: 运动时大脑释放让人产生幸福感的化学物质。

questions.question: How much exercise do experts recommend weekly?
questions.explanation: 专家建议每周至少 150 分钟的中等强度活动。

title: Studying Abroad
passage: Studying abroad is a life-changing experience for many students, but it comes with both rewards and challenges. On the positive side, students gain independence, improve their language skills, and develop a global perspective that employers value. However, living in a foreign country can also be difficult, as students face homesickness, culture shock, and financial pressure. Experts advise students to prepare carefully, set realistic expectations, and stay open to new experiences.

questions.question: What is a benefit of studying abroad?
questions.explanation: 留学能让学生获得独立、提高语言能力并培养全球视野。

questions.question: What challenge do students face abroad?
questions.explanation: 学生在国外会面临想家、文化冲击和经济压力。

questions.question: What do experts advise students to do?
questions.explanation: 专家建议学生认真准备、设合理预期并对新体验保持开放。

title: The Ageing Population
passage: Many countries are experiencing a rapid ageing of their populations as birth rates fall and life expectancy rises. This demographic shift brings significant challenges, including increased demand for healthcare and pressure on pension systems. At the same time, an ageing population can be seen as an opportunity: older people bring experience, wisdom, and often a willingness to volunteer. Societies that adapt well will find ways to keep older citizens active and engaged.

questions.question: What causes the ageing of populations?
options: Falling birth rates and longer lives
questions.explanation: 出生率下降和预期寿命延长导致人口老龄化。

questions.question: What challenge does ageing bring?
questions.explanation: 老龄化增加了医疗需求和养老金体系的压力。

questions.question: What opportunity does ageing present?
options: Older people bring experience and wisdom
questions.explanation: 老年人带来经验、智慧，并常常愿意做志愿工作。

title: The Psychology of Consumer Choice
passage: Marketers have long understood that consumer decisions are rarely purely rational. Shoppers are influenced by a wide range of psychological factors, from the colour of packaging to the way prices are displayed. For example, an item priced at 9.99 appears significantly cheaper than one priced at 10, even though the difference is trivial. Understanding these influences can help consumers make more deliberate choices rather than being guided entirely by emotion or clever marketing.

questions.question: What have marketers long understood?
options: Consumer decisions are rarely purely rational
questions.explanation: 营销人员早就明白消费者的决定很少是纯理性的。

questions.question: Why does 9.99 seem much cheaper than 10?
options: Because it is a bigger discount
questions.explanation: 价格显示方式带来的心理效应让 9.99 显得便宜得多。

questions.question: What can understanding these influences help consumers do?
questions.explanation: 理解这些影响能帮助消费者做出更审慎的选择。

title: The Decline of Handwriting
passage: As keyboards and touchscreens replace pens, handwriting is quietly disappearing from daily life. This change carries unexpected consequences. Research shows that writing by hand activates areas of the brain involved in memory and learning in ways that typing does not. Students who take notes by hand tend to understand and retain material better than those who type. Some educators therefore argue that handwriting should remain part of the curriculum, not out of nostalgia, but for its genuine cognitive benefits.

questions.question: What is quietly disappearing from daily life?
questions.explanation: 随着键盘和触屏取代笔，手写正从日常生活中消失。

questions.question: What does writing by hand activate?
options: Areas of the brain involved in memory
questions.explanation: 手写能激活大脑中与记忆和学习相关的区域。

questions.question: Why do some educators want to keep handwriting in the curriculum?
questions.explanation: 教育者认为应保留手写，是因为它真正的认知益处而非怀旧。

title: The Economics of Happiness
passage: The relationship between money and happiness is more complicated than most people assume. Research shows that rising income does improve well-being, but only up to a point. Once basic needs are met, additional wealth produces smaller and smaller gains in satisfaction. What predicts happiness far more reliably are relationships, health, and a sense of purpose. This finding has led some governments to look beyond economic growth and to measure the well-being of their citizens directly.

questions.question: According to the passage, rising income improves well-being only until what point?
questions.explanation: 收入增长只在基本需求满足之前显著提升幸福感。

questions.question: What predicts happiness more reliably than money?
questions.explanation: 关系、健康和目标感比金钱更能预测幸福。

questions.question: What have some governments begun to measure?
questions.explanation: 一些政府开始直接衡量公民的幸福感。

title: The Benefits of Bilingualism
passage: Bilingualism was once viewed with suspicion, but research has turned that view on its head. Far from confusing the mind, speaking two languages appears to strengthen it. Bilingual individuals constantly manage two linguistic systems, which exercises the brain's executive control and improves attention. Some studies even suggest that lifelong bilingualism may delay the onset of dementia by several years, building a cognitive reserve that protects the ageing brain.

questions.question: How was bilingualism once viewed?
questions.explanation: 双语能力曾被怀疑地看待。

questions.question: What does speaking two languages strengthen?
questions.explanation: 双语者不断管理两套语言系统，锻炼了大脑的执行控制能力。

questions.question: What may lifelong bilingualism delay?
questions.explanation: 研究表明终身双语可能将痴呆症发病推迟数年。

title: The Growth Mindset
passage: The growth mindset is the belief that abilities can be developed through effort and learning. People with this mindset tend to see challenges as opportunities rather than threats, and they persist longer when facing difficulty. In contrast, those with a fixed mindset believe that intelligence is innate and unchangeable, which can lead them to avoid challenges for fear of failure. The key insight, educators say, is that praising effort rather than talent encourages the kind of persistence that leads to genuine improvement.

questions.question: What is the growth mindset?
options: The belief that abilities can be developed
The belief that intelligence is fixed
questions.explanation: 成长型思维是相信能力可以通过努力和学习发展。

questions.question: What do people with a fixed mindset tend to do?
options: Avoid challenges for fear of failure
questions.explanation: 固定型思维的人认为智力天生不变，可能因害怕失败而回避挑战。

questions.question: What should educators praise to encourage persistence?
questions.explanation: 教育者应表扬努力而非天赋，以鼓励坚持。

title: The Importance of Critical Thinking
passage: In an age of information overload, critical thinking has become an essential skill. It is the ability to evaluate evidence, question assumptions, and distinguish fact from opinion. Schools have traditionally focused on delivering knowledge, but educators increasingly argue that teaching students how to think is more important than teaching them what to think. A person who can think critically is less easily misled and better equipped to make sound decisions in a complex world.

questions.question: What is critical thinking?
questions.explanation: 批判性思维是评估证据、质疑假设和区分事实与观点的能力。

questions.question: What do educators increasingly argue?
options: Teaching how to think is more important than what to think
questions.explanation: 教育者认为教学生如何思考比教他们思考什么更重要。

questions.question: What is a benefit of critical thinking?
questions.explanation: 能批判性思考的人不易被误导，更能做出明智的决定。

title: The Value of Failure
passage: Failure is rarely welcome, yet it is one of the most effective teachers. Many of history's greatest achievements were built on repeated setbacks, from scientific discoveries to entrepreneurial success. The key difference between those who grow from failure and those who are defeated by it lies in how they respond. People who examine their mistakes, learn from them, and try again tend to build the resilience that eventually leads to success. In this sense, failure is not the opposite of success but a necessary step on the road to it.

questions.question: What is one of the most effective teachers according to the passage?
questions.explanation: 失败是最有效的老师之一。

questions.question: What is the key difference between those who grow and those who are defeated?
questions.explanation: 关键区别在于人们如何回应失败。

questions.question: What does failure eventually lead to for those who learn from it?
questions.explanation: 从失败中学习的人会培养出最终通向成功的韧性。

title: The Nature of Metaphor
passage: Metaphor is often thought of as a decorative device used by poets, but linguists argue that it is far more fundamental. In their view, metaphor shapes the way we think, not just the way we speak. We speak of time as money, of arguments as buildings, and of life as a journey, and these metaphors quietly structure our understanding. Once we recognise how deeply metaphorical thinking runs, we begin to see that language is never merely literal.

questions.question: How is metaphor often thought of?
options: As a decorative device for poets
questions.explanation: 隐喻常被视为诗人使用的装饰手法。

questions.question: What do linguists argue about metaphor?
options: It shapes the way we think
questions.explanation: 语言学家认为隐喻塑造了我们的思维方式。

questions.question: What do we speak of time as?
questions.explanation: 我们把时间说成金钱（如节省时间、花费时间）。

title: Translation and Cultural Equivalence
passage: One of the central problems in translation theory is the question of equivalence. A translator must decide whether to remain faithful to the literal meaning of the original or to reproduce its effect in the target culture. A phrase that is perfectly natural in one language may sound awkward or even meaningless in another. Skilled translators therefore navigate between languages and cultures, often sacrificing literal accuracy to preserve the spirit, tone, and function of the original text.

questions.question: What is a central problem in translation theory?
questions.explanation: 翻译理论的核心问题之一是对等问题。

questions.question: What must a translator decide between?
questions.explanation: 译者要在忠实原文字面和再现其文化效果之间抉择。

questions.question: What may skilled translators sacrifice?
questions.explanation: 熟练的译者可能牺牲字面准确以保留原文精神、语气和功能。

title: The Stream of Consciousness
passage: The stream of consciousness is a narrative technique that attempts to capture the flow of thoughts and feelings as they pass through a character's mind. Unlike traditional narration, which presents events in an orderly way, this technique mirrors the chaotic, associative nature of thought itself. Writers such as Virginia Woolf and James Joyce used it to explore the inner lives of their characters with unprecedented depth, though their prose can be demanding for readers.

questions.question: What does the stream of consciousness attempt to capture?
options: The flow of thoughts and feelings
questions.explanation: 意识流试图捕捉人物脑海中思绪和情感的流动。

questions.question: How does this technique differ from traditional narration?
options: It mirrors the chaotic nature of thought
questions.explanation: 它模仿思想本身混乱、联想式的特征。

questions.question: Which writers are mentioned?
questions.explanation: 文中提到弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫和詹姆斯·乔伊斯。

title: Language and Thought
passage: Does the language we speak shape the way we think? This question, known as the Sapir-Whorf hypothesis, has fascinated linguists for decades. In its strong form, the hypothesis claims that language determines thought, while its weaker version suggests that language merely influences it. Most scholars today accept a moderate position: language does not imprison the mind, but the words and categories a language offers can highlight some distinctions and obscure others.

questions.question: What is the Sapir-Whorf hypothesis about?
questions.explanation: 萨丕尔-沃尔夫假说探讨语言是否塑造思维。

questions.question: What does the strong form of the hypothesis claim?
questions.explanation: 强式假说认为语言决定思维。

questions.question: What position do most scholars accept today?
questions.explanation: 大多数学者接受温和立场：语言不囚禁思维，但会凸显或模糊某些区别。

title: The Role of Symbolism in Literature
passage: Symbolism is a literary device in which an object, person, or event represents a deeper meaning beyond its literal sense. In F. Scott Fitzgerald's The Great Gatsby, the green light across the bay symbolises Gatsby's dreams and the broader American Dream. Symbols gain their power from context and repetition, and their interpretation often requires careful reading. A symbol is not merely a hidden code but a way of layering additional meaning onto a text.

questions.question: What is symbolism?
options: A device where something represents a deeper meaning
questions.explanation: 象征是物体、人物或事件代表字面之外更深含义的文学手法。

questions.question: What does the green light symbolise in The Great Gatsby?
options: Gatsby's dreams and the American Dream
questions.explanation: 绿灯象征盖茨比的梦想和更广泛的美国梦。

questions.question: How do symbols gain their power?
questions.explanation: 象征的力量来自语境和重复，其解读需要仔细阅读。

title: The Concept of the Canon
passage: The literary canon refers to the body of works traditionally regarded as the most important and worthy of study. For much of history, this canon was dominated by a narrow group of writers, and critics have long debated who gets included and who is left out. In recent decades, scholars have worked to broaden the canon, bringing in voices that were previously marginalised. The debate over the canon is ultimately a debate about what a culture chooses to remember and value.

questions.question: What is the literary canon?
options: Works traditionally regarded as most important
questions.explanation: 文学经典是传统上被认为最重要、最值得研究的作品整体。

questions.question: What have critics debated?
options: Who gets included and left out
questions.explanation: 批评家长期争论谁被收录、谁被排除。

questions.question: What is the debate over the canon ultimately about?
options: What a culture chooses to remember and value
questions.explanation: 关于经典的争论本质上是关于一个文化选择记住和珍视什么。

title: First and Second Language Acquisition
passage: Linguists distinguish between first language acquisition, the natural process by which children learn their mother tongue, and second language acquisition, which occurs when a person learns another language later in life. Children acquire their first language largely through immersion and without formal instruction, while adults often learn a second language more consciously, relying on rules and memorisation. Understanding the differences helps explain why adults rarely achieve native-like pronunciation, even when they achieve fluency.

questions.question: How do children acquire their first language?
questions.explanation: 儿童主要通过沉浸、无需正式教学来习得母语。

questions.question: How do adults often learn a second language?
questions.explanation: 成年人学习第二语言更靠自觉，依赖规则和记忆。

questions.question: What do adults rarely achieve even when fluent?
questions.explanation: 即使达到流利，成年人也很少能达到母语者的发音。

title: The Essay as a Literary Form
passage: The essay is a remarkably flexible literary form, sitting somewhere between literature and journalism, between the personal and the philosophical. It was popularised by the French writer Montaigne, who used it to explore his own thoughts in a tentative, questioning manner. Unlike a formal treatise, which aims to prove a point, the essay often proceeds by exploration, circling around an idea rather than marching toward a conclusion. This openness is precisely what gives the essay its enduring appeal.

questions.question: Where does the essay sit?
questions.explanation: 散文是介于文学与新闻、个人与哲思之间的灵活文体。

questions.question: Who popularised the essay?
questions.explanation: 法国作家蒙田使散文这一文体流行起来。

questions.question: How does the essay often proceed?
questions.explanation: 散文常以探索方式推进，围绕一个想法盘旋而非直奔结论。

title: Ambiguity in Poetry
passage: Ambiguity in poetry is not a flaw but often a source of richness. When a line of verse can be read in more than one way, it invites the reader to participate in creating meaning. The critic William Empson identified several types of ambiguity, showing how multiple interpretations can coexist within a single phrase. This openness, however, places demands on the reader, who must weigh competing readings rather than settle for a single, fixed interpretation.

questions.question: What is ambiguity in poetry often a source of?
questions.explanation: 诗歌中的歧义不是缺陷，而往往是丰富的来源。

questions.question: What does ambiguous verse invite the reader to do?
questions.explanation: 歧义的诗句邀请读者参与意义的创造。

questions.question: Who identified types of ambiguity?
questions.explanation: 批评家威廉·燕卜荪识别出多种歧义类型。

title: Irony and Its Functions
passage: Irony is one of the most powerful and frequently misunderstood devices in literature. In its simplest form, it occurs when what is said differs from what is meant. Dramatic irony arises when the audience knows something that a character does not, creating tension and often pathos. Because irony depends on a gap between appearance and reality, it rewards readers who pay close attention, and it can serve purposes ranging from gentle humour to sharp social criticism.

questions.question: What is irony in its simplest form?
options: When what is said differs from what is meant
questions.explanation: 反讽最简形式是所说与所表达的意思不同。

questions.question: What is dramatic irony?
options: When the audience knows something a character does not
questions.explanation: 戏剧性反讽指观众知道角色所不知之事。

questions.question: What can irony serve?
options: From gentle humour to sharp criticism
questions.explanation: 反讽可用于温和幽默到尖锐社会批判等多种目的。

title: The Translator as Mediator
passage: The traditional view of the translator as an invisible servant has been challenged by modern translation studies. Scholars now see the translator as a mediator who actively negotiates between two languages and two cultures. Far from being a mechanical converter of words, the translator makes countless interpretive choices that shape how readers understand a foreign text. This recognition has raised the status of translation from a mere craft to a creative and intellectual activity in its own right.

questions.question: How was the translator traditionally viewed?
options: As an equal to the author
questions.explanation: 传统观点把译者视为隐形的仆人。

questions.question: How do modern scholars see the translator?
options: As a mediator between languages and cultures
questions.explanation: 现代学者把译者视为两种语言和两种文化之间的协调者。

questions.question: What has the recognition of the translator raised translation to?
questions.explanation: 这种认识把翻译从单纯技艺提升为创造性和智识活动。

title: Narrative Point of View
passage: The choice of narrative point of view fundamentally shapes a story. A first-person narrator offers intimacy but limits the reader to a single perspective, while a third-person omniscient narrator can move freely among characters but sacrifices some immediacy. Between these poles lie many variations, such as the limited third person, which follows one character closely while remaining outside them. Authors choose their point of view with care, knowing that it determines what readers can see and, crucially, what they cannot.

questions.question: What does a first-person narrator offer?
questions.explanation: 第一人称叙述提供亲密感，但把读者限制在单一视角。

questions.question: What does an omniscient narrator sacrifice?
questions.explanation: 全知叙述者能自由移动于人物之间，但牺牲了一些即时感。

questions.question: What does narrative point of view determine?
options: What readers can see and cannot see
questions.explanation: 叙述视角决定了读者能看到什么、看不到什么。
